text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Fuel shortage has gripped Nigeria's administrative capital Abuja, with long queues outside the few filling stations still selling fuel.
- The Petroleum Trust Fund says it will repair dilapidated structures at Nigeria's universities and polytechnics. Work will begin in September.
- Royal Dutch/Shell has completed a second seismic survey in the northern region around Bauchi. Company officials said the surveys will establish the best prospects for oil drilling.
- Cash-strapped investors are forcing down the prices of blue chip shares, as they try to dump them as quickly as possible.
- More than 45 companies are hoping to participate in developing marginal oil fields, raising hopes for increased competition in the sector.
- Increasing numbers of filling stations are being offered for sale in the commercial capital Lagos, as sporadic fuel crises eat into takings.
- Directors of Central Insurance Company are expected to present a proposal to raise its capital base to 200 million naira from 100 million naira.
- A vital component of the northern Kaduna oil refinery has broken.
- Top aides of military ruler General Sani Abacha are positioning themselves to bid for the presidency if pressure persuades the head of state not to stand in 1998 elections.
- The price of rice is expected to ease following the arrival in Lagos of around one million 50 kg bags.
